collection.description: After every theory of towers and machines, a child asks whether an unknown family might simply be cooking supper.

setup.name: The setup
setup.text: After hearing every theory of towers, machines, and distant customs, a child asks whether an unknown family might simply be cooking supper.

a1.name: Outcome A1
a1.text: The villagers picture a parent coaxing a tired child to eat.

a2.name: Outcome A2
a2.text: A solitary elder imagines someone far away enjoying supper alone.

b1.name: Outcome B1
b1.text: A researcher says distant people might eat unfamiliar food in unfamiliar homes.

text_only.reason: food talked about or imagined; the village's stores do not change

b2.name: Outcome B2
b2.text: A storyteller adds that difference in custom need not mean difference in feeling.

c1.name: Outcome C1
c1.text: The council records its questions as guesses, not discoveries.

c2.name: Outcome C2
c2.text: The child asks whether distant people might also be wondering whether Isolans laugh, grieve, and dream.
